environment.title: Environment interaction map
environment.principle: Plant response comes from interacting conditions, not isolated numbers. Read the canopy, air, root zone, and recent change together.

factors.label: Light / PPFD
factors.summary: Light drives photosynthesis but also adds leaf heat load. Distribution across the canopy matters as much as a single reading.

factors.label: Leaf temperature
factors.summary: Leaf temperature can differ from room temperature and directly influences vapor pressure at the leaf surface.

factors.label: Air temperature
factors.summary: Air temperature affects metabolism and the vapor-pressure relationship that shapes atmospheric drying demand.

factors.label: Relative humidity
factors.summary: Relative humidity describes how close air is to saturation at its current temperature and must be interpreted with temperature.

factors.label: VPD
factors.summary: Vapor pressure deficit is a useful description of evaporative demand between leaf and air, not a diagnosis by itself.

factors.label: Airflow
factors.summary: Air movement changes the leaf boundary layer and influences heat and vapor exchange around foliage.

factors.label: CO₂
factors.summary: Carbon dioxide availability interacts with light, stomatal behavior, temperature, and plant capacity for photosynthesis.

factors.label: Root-zone water
factors.summary: Water availability must be interpreted with substrate aeration, root condition, container volume, and atmospheric demand.

factors.label: Root oxygen
factors.summary: Roots require oxygen for respiration. Persistent saturation can reduce gas exchange even when water is abundant.

factors.label: pH
factors.summary: Root-zone pH influences chemical form and availability of nutrients, but must be read with media type, irrigation, and EC.

factors.label: EC
factors.summary: Electrical conductivity estimates dissolved ionic concentration. Trend, runoff context, source water, and substrate matter.

diagnostics.title: Whole-plant symptom locator
diagnostics.principle: Location is evidence. Record where a symptom starts, how it is patterned, and how it changes before ranking possible causes.

zones.label: Newest growth
questions: Is new growth pale, distorted, twisted, or stalled?
Are veins and tissue affected differently?
Is damage symmetrical across growing tips?
What changed in root-zone pH, EC, environment, or inputs?

zones.label: Upper canopy
questions: Is damage strongest nearest the light source?
Do leaf edges taco upward or bleach?
Is leaf temperature elevated?
Is only the exposed canopy affected?

zones.label: Middle canopy
questions: Is the pattern spreading upward or downward?
Is spotting random, interveinal, marginal, or tip-focused?
Are pests or residues visible on leaf undersides?
Are multiple branches equally affected?

zones.label: Older / lower leaves
questions: Did symptoms begin on the oldest leaves?
Is yellowing uniform or between veins?
Are margins, tips, or entire leaves affected?
Is the plant reallocating mobile nutrients during rapid growth or senescence?

zones.label: One branch / sector
questions: Is the rest of the plant normal?
Is there local stem damage or restriction?
Are pests, infection, or physical injury localized?
Does irrigation reach this sector equally?

zones.label: Whole plant
questions: Was onset sudden or gradual?
Is the media too wet or too dry?
Did environment, irrigation, feed strength, or lighting change recently?
Are roots healthy and are measurements credible?

zones.label: Root zone
questions: What is substrate moisture now and over the last cycle?
Is there adequate aeration and drainage?
What are pH and EC trends?
Are roots white/tan and firm, or dark/soft with odor or sloughing?
